title: Brad Bird Reveals Chinatown's Influence on Ray Gunn
excerpt:
Jack Nicholson's detective performance helped shape Bird's animated protagonist.
Ray Gunn premieres on Netflix on December 18, 2026.
body_md:
Brad Bird, director of The Iron Giant and The Incredibles, is finally bringing his long-developed animated detective project Ray Gunn to audiences. Its retro science-fiction aesthetic evokes magazines from the 1930s, but the central character draws heavily on film noir.

Bird cited Humphrey Bogart classics including The Maltese Falcon and The Big Sleep, while identifying Roman Polanski's Chinatown as his favorite detective film. Jack Nicholson's portrayal of private investigator J.J. Gittes was particularly influential in developing Ray's personality.

The filmmaker singled out Nicholson's willingness to spend much of Chinatown wearing a prominent nose bandage. Bird admired the actor's lack of vanity and commitment to the consequences of his character's curiosity. For Ray's physical appearance, the team looked toward a young Montgomery Clift, especially his striking eyebrows and facial features.

The combination of detective fiction and a world populated by aliens and robots invites comparisons with Who Framed Roger Rabbit, although that is a critical parallel rather than a claim of direct adaptation. Bird has repeatedly explored mature themes through animation, including family tensions and personal dissatisfaction in The Incredibles.

He also expressed openness to directing an R-rated animated film if the right story emerged, without announcing a specific project. Ray Gunn opens in select theaters on December 4, 2026, before its Netflix debut on December 18.
